units.title: Introduction to Science
units.intro: This unit is about what science is, the scientific method, and measuring with units.

cards.title: What is science?
body: **Science** is a body of knowledge.
It is careful **observation**, **experiments** and **conclusions**.
It is a way to study our **environment**.

cards.title: Our environment
body: The **environment** is the world around us.
People, plants, animals, rivers and mountains are part of it.

cards.title: Three branches of science
body: Science has **three main branches**. Tap the dots.

cards.title: Memory trick: P C B
body: Say: **P**lease **C**hoose **B**ooks.

cards.title: Who is a scientist?
body: A **scientist** is a person who studies science.
Scientists study **why** and **how** things change.
They follow the **scientific method**.

cards.title: How scientists work
body: They ask: why? how? when? what?
They read books, ask people and do experiments.
They **observe** carefully.

cards.q: Which one is NOT a branch of science?
cards.why: The three branches are Physics, Chemistry and Biology (p. 2).

cards.title: The five steps

steps.text: **1. Identify the problem.** A problem is a question with no answer yet.
**2. Collect information.** Observe: look and think carefully.
**3. Make a hypothesis.** A hypothesis is a **scientific guess**. It can be right or wrong.
**4. Do an experiment.** This tests the hypothesis.
**5. Make a conclusion.** It shows if the hypothesis is right or not.

body: Tap Next to climb the steps.

body: The five steps, in order.

cards.title: A hypothesis
body: A **hypothesis** is a scientific guess.
It comes from observations.
It must be **proved** by an experiment.

cards.title: Worked example: a dying plant

steps.text: **Problem:** why is the plant dying?
**Observation:** the plant is dying.
**Hypothesis:** it gets too little water.
**Experiment:** give it more water.
**Conclusion:** the plant was dying because it got too little water.

**Hypothesis:** the doctors guessed **malaria or meningitis**.
**Experiment:** they tested blood in a **laboratory**.
**Conclusion:** it was **meningitis**. Medicine cured the people.

body: People use the scientific method to solve problems.

body: Most people use a **metre** for length, a **beam balance** for mass and a **watch** for time.
Scientific measurements are **accurate**.
They all have **units**.

cards.title: What is a unit?
body: A **unit** is an amount used as a standard of measurement.
Example: the **metre** is a unit of length.

body: A **standard unit** is agreed by all countries.
**Metre (m)**, **kilogram (kg)** and **second (s)** are **SI units**.
SI is also called the **Metric System**.

cards.title: What does SI mean?

In English it is the **International System**.
Most countries use SI units.

Some objects are **moving**.
**Motion** is a change of position.

cards.title: Distance
body: **Distance** is how far an object moves.
It is the length of the road between two points.
The SI unit of distance is the **metre (m)**.

cards.title: Speed
body: **Speed** tells how fast or slowly something moves.
Speed = distance ÷ time.
Short form: **v = S ÷ t**

cards.title: Force

The SI unit of force is the **newton (N)**.

cards.title: Types of force
body: gravity, friction, elastic force, magnetic force and electrostatic force.
This unit looks at **gravity** and **friction**.

cards.title: Gravity
body: The earth **pulls** objects towards it.
This pull is **gravity** (gravitational force).

cards.title: Mass
body: **Mass** is how much material an object has.
It is the **same everywhere**, on the earth or the moon.
Measure it with a **beam balance**, in **kilograms (kg)**.

cards.title: Other units of mass
body: grams (g) and tonnes.
1 tonne = 1000 kg.
The SI unit is the **kilogram**.

cards.title: Weight
body: **Weight** is a **force**: the pull of gravity on an object.
Measure it with a **spring balance**, in **newtons (N)**.
Weight **changes** from place to place.

cards.title: Friction
body: When surfaces **rub**, there is a force between them.
This force is **friction**.
Friction **opposes** and **slows down** motion.

A problem

states.text: **Sliding friction**: one surface **slides** over another.

cards.title: Two big kinds
body: **Static** friction: surfaces at rest.
**Dynamic** friction: surfaces moving. It is **sliding** or **rolling**.

cards.title: Memory trick: S-S-R
body: **S**till, **S**lide, **R**oll.

cards.title: Examples

cards.title: Three ways to reduce friction
body: **Oil** the surfaces (bicycles, sewing machines).
Use **ball or roller bearings** (wheels on suitcases).
**Polish** the surfaces (smooth slides for children).

cards.title: Rolling beats sliding
body: **Rolling friction is much less than sliding friction.**
So rollers and balls make things move easily.

units.title: Matter and Energy
units.intro: This unit is about matter, its states, energy and its types, energy changes and saving energy.

cards.title: Matter
body: Everything around us is **matter**.
Matter **takes up space** and **has mass**.
Living and non-living things are matter. Even air!

cards.title: Natural or artificial?
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Natural
states.text: **Natural** materials come from nature: cotton, oranges, wood.

states.label: Artificial
states.text: **Artificial** (man-made) materials are made by people: plastic, nails, pens.

cards.title: Three states
body: **Solid, liquid** and **gas** are the states of matter.
Heating or cooling can change the state.
The space matter takes up is its **volume**.

cards.title: Shape and volume (Figure 4.2)
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Solid
states.text: A **solid** has a definite **shape** and a definite **volume**.

states.label: Liquid
states.text: A **liquid** has **no** definite shape, but a definite volume.

states.label: Gas
states.text: A **gas** has **no** definite shape and **no** definite volume.

**Cooling** condenses steam and freezes water.

cards.title: Did you know?
body: Water boils at **100 °C** at sea level.
On top of Mount Everest it boils at only about **70 °C**.

cards.title: Energy
body: **Energy** is the ability to **do work**.
It can change the temperature, shape, speed, position or direction of things.
The SI unit is the **joule (J)**.

cards.title: Fuels and food
body: Wood, coal, kerosene and Butagas are **fuels**.
Fuels and food have **stored energy**.

cards.title: Sources of light
body: Anything that gives out light is a **source of light**.
There are **natural** and **man-made** sources.

cards.title: Natural or man-made? (Figure 5.1)
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Natural
states.text: The sun, stars, fire-flies and some fish give out light **from their bodies**. The **sun** is the main source.

states.label: Man-made
states.text: Candles, oil-lamps, camp-fires, torches and electric bulbs. They are also called **artificial** sources.

cards.q: Which is a natural source of light?

cards.title: Activity 5.1: three cards
body: Move the slider.

states.label: In a line
states.text: All holes in a straight line: you see the candle.

states.label: One moved
states.text: Move one card: you cannot see the light.

cards.title: Light travels in a straight line
body: A **ray** is one straight line with an arrow. It shows the direction of light.
A **beam** is a group of parallel rays.

cards.title: Ray or beam? (Figure 5.3)
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Ray
states.text: One line with an arrow.

states.label: Beam
states.text: Many parallel rays.

cards.title: Transmission
body: **Transmission** means letting light pass through.
A glass window **transmits** light.

cards.title: Three kinds of materials
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Transparent
states.text: **Transparent**: lets **all** the light through. Air, clear plastic.

states.label: Translucent
states.text: **Translucent**: lets **part** of the light through. Thin plastic, smoked glass, muddy water.

states.label: Opaque
states.text: **Opaque**: lets **no** light through. Wood, coal tar, paint, metal sheets.

cards.title: Memory trick: All, Part, None
body: Opaque is like a big **O**: nothing gets through.

cards.title: Shadows
body: A **shadow** forms when an **opaque** object blocks light.
Shadows form because light travels in **straight lines**.

cards.title: Formation of shadows (Figure 5.4)
body: Activity 5.3: a ball between a light and a screen. Tap the dots.

cards.title: Two parts of a shadow
body: **Umbra**: the inner, dark part.
**Penumbra**: the outer, less dark part.

cards.title: Moving in space
body: The earth moves round the sun.
The moon moves round the earth.
Sometimes the sun, earth and moon are in a **straight line**.

cards.title: Eclipse
body: An **eclipse** happens when one body moves in front of another and blocks sunlight.
There are **solar** and **lunar** eclipses.

cards.title: Solar or lunar? (Figures 5.5 and 5.6)
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Solar
states.text: **Solar eclipse**: the **moon** passes between the sun and the earth. The moon's shadow falls on the earth.

states.label: Lunar
states.text: **Lunar eclipse**: the **earth** passes between the sun and the moon. The earth's shadow falls on the moon.

cards.title: Memory trick: who is in the Middle?
body: **Lunar** = **Luna** (moon) gets dark.

cards.title: A pin-hole camera (Figure 5.7)
body: Activity 5.4. Tap the dots.

cards.title: Pin-hole camera
body: A **pin-hole camera** is a simple device.
It forms an **image** of an object on a screen.
The figure shows the image **upside down**.

cards.title: Make one
body: Make a tiny hole in one side of a box.
Line the box with black paper.
Cover the open side with oiled paper: the screen.

cards.title: Reflection
body: When light **bounces back** from a surface, it is **reflection**.
There are **regular** and **irregular** reflections.

cards.title: Regular or irregular? (Figure 5.9)
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Regular
states.text: Parallel rays hit a **smooth, flat** surface. They go back **parallel**, in one direction.

states.label: Irregular
states.text: Parallel rays hit a **rough** surface. They go back in **different directions**.

cards.title: Mirrors
body: A **mirror** is a highly polished surface that reflects light.
There are **plane** (flat) and **curved** mirrors.

cards.title: Reflection at a plane mirror (Figure 5.10)
body: Tap each part.

Meaning

steps.text: Look in a mirror. Raise your **right** hand.
Your image raises its **left** hand. Right and left are **swapped**.

body: Tap Next.

cards.title: Curved mirrors (Figure 5.12)
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Concave
states.text: **Concave**: the **inner** surface of the curve is the mirror.

states.label: Convex
states.text: **Convex**: the **outer** surface of the curve is the mirror.

cards.title: Memory trick: con-CAVE
body: You go **in** to a cave.

body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: Periscope
body: A long tube with a **plane mirror** at each end.
The mirrors are **parallel** and at **45°**.
Light goes: object → top mirror → bottom mirror → eye.

cards.title: Uses
body: See over the heads of a crowd.
See over a wall.
**Submarines** use it to see above the sea.

cards.title: Activity 5.8: a stick in water (Figure 5.14)
body: The stick looks **bent**. It is not really bent! Tap the dots.

cards.title: Refraction
body: A **medium** is a material light can travel through.
Light **bends** when it goes from one transparent medium into another.
This bending is **refraction**.

cards.title: Why does light bend?
body: Its **speed changes**.
Light is **slower** in water than in air.
In air, light travels 300 million m/s (3 × 10⁸ m/s).

cards.title: A prism
body: A **prism** is a piece of glass (or other transparent material) with flat faces.
It usually has **five** faces.

cards.title: Activity 5.9: dispersion (Figure 5.15)
body: White light goes into the prism. Tap the colours.

cards.title: Dispersion and spectrum
body: **Dispersion**: white light splits into its colours.
The band of colours is a **spectrum**.
It has **seven** colours.

cards.title: Memory trick: ROY G BIV
body: Say it like a name: **Roy G. Biv**.

cards.title: Activity 5.10: a colour disc (Figure 5.16)
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Still
states.text: Paint 7 equal parts in the 7 colours.

states.label: Spinning
states.text: Spin it fast. The colours mix and look almost white.

cards.title: A rainbow (Figure 5.17)
body: Sunlight shines on raindrops. The drops act like **prisms**. Tap the dots.

cards.title: Rainbow
body: A **rainbow** is a coloured arc in the sky.
It is a **spectrum of sunlight**.
Raindrops split sunlight into **seven colours**.

cards.title: Lens
body: A **lens** is transparent and has **curved** surfaces.
A lens **refracts** light. (A mirror reflects.)

cards.title: Two types of lenses
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Convex
states.text: **Convex**: thicker in the middle. Rays **converge** (meet). Also called a **converging** lens.

states.label: Concave
states.text: **Concave**: thinner in the middle. Rays **diverge** (spread). Also called a **diverging** lens.

cards.title: Activity 5.11: a magnifying glass
body: Hold it over paper in sunlight.
Move it until you get a small, sharp spot of light.
A magnifying glass is a convex lens: it brings rays together.

cards.title: Uses of lenses
body: eye glasses, cameras, microscopes and telescopes

cards.title: Wind

**Moving air** is called **wind**.
You cannot see air, but you can see and hear wind in the trees.

cards.title: Oxygen and water vapour
body: **Oxygen** is important for life. Without it, there is no life.
Lots of water vapour in the air makes the weather **humid**.

cards.title: Activity 6.3: oxygen in the air (Figure 6.3)

steps.text: Put a candle in a bowl of water and light it.
Cover it with a glass.
The candle uses up the oxygen and goes out. The water rises about **20%**. So oxygen is about **20%** of the air.

cards.title: The fire triangle (Figure 6.5)
body: Fire needs **three** things. Tap the dots.

cards.title: Fire needs three things
body: **Fuel**, **heat** and **air (oxygen)**.
If one is missing, the fire **goes out**.

cards.title: Memory trick: F H A
body: **F**ire **H**as **A**ll three.

cards.title: Fire helps and harms
body: We need fire to cook and to stay warm.
We burn wood, kerosene or butagas.
But fire is dangerous. Handle it with care.

cards.title: Did you know? Bottles and fire
body: Do not leave bottles near grass, paper or fuel.
A bottle can act as a **lens** and focus the sun's rays. This can start a fire.

cards.title: Fighting fire
body: To put out a fire, take away **one** of the three. Move the slider.

states.label: Fuel
states.text: No fuel: the fire goes out.

states.label: Heat
states.text: No heat: the fire goes out.

states.label: Air

cards.title: Air for life
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Breathe in
states.text: We **breathe in oxygen** from the air.

states.label: Breathe out
states.text: We **breathe out carbon dioxide**.

cards.title: We cannot live without air
body: Oxygen **burns our food** to give energy.
All animals and plants need air.
People can live a month without food, a week without water, but only a **few minutes** without air.

cards.q: Which is NOT needed for a fire?
cards.why: Fire needs fuel, heat and air (oxygen) (p. 88).

cards.title: The atmosphere
body: The **atmosphere** is the layer of air around the Earth.
The book says it is about **800 km** thick.
The air gets **thinner** as you go up.

cards.title: The atmosphere (Figure 6.8)
body: Tap the dots.

cards.title: High places
body: It is harder to breathe high up. There is less oxygen.
Mount Everest is **8845 m** high (the book's number). Climbers take extra oxygen.

cards.title: Did you know?
body: The atmosphere protects the earth.
By day it protects us from the sun's burning heat.
At night it is like a **blanket**: it keeps the heat in.

cards.title: Pressure
body: Pressure depends on **weight** and **area**.
Big weight on a small area: **more** pressure.
Small weight on a large area: **less** pressure.

cards.title: Weight and area

states.label: Less

cards.title: Air pressure
body: The **weight of air** pushes on the Earth. This is **air pressure**.
It changes from day to day.
It is used in **weather forecasts**.

steps.text: Put a bowl of water on a table and a glass on a chair, lower down.
Put a pipe from the bowl to the glass. Suck the air out.
Water flows into the glass. A **difference in air pressure** makes it flow.

body: Tap Next.

Pollution harms living things.

cards.title: Reducing pollution

lessons.title: The Cell: Basic Unit of Life

cards.title: The cell
body: All living things are made of **cells**.
Cells are the **building blocks** of the body.
A cell is the **basic unit of life**.

cards.title: How many cells?
body: A human body has **thousands of millions** of cells.
A housefly has **millions** of cells.
Like stones in a wall, cells build a body (Figure 7.2).

cards.title: Seeing cells
body: Cells are too small to see with our eyes.
A **hand lens** does not magnify enough.
We need a **microscope**.

cards.title: Did you know?
body: In **1665**, **Robert Hooke** was the first to see cells with a microscope.
They looked like a **honeycomb**.

cards.title: Basic contents of a cell
body: **Cell membrane**, **cytoplasm** and **nucleus**.
These parts are called **organelles**.
An organelle has a special job.

body: Tap each part.

body: Tap each part.

cards.title: Cell division
body: Cells grow and **divide into two**.
This is **cell division**.

cards.title: Let us think
body: Someone knocks at the door. What do you do?
You feel thirsty. What do you do?
You are reacting to a **change**.

cards.title: Stimulus
body: A **stimulus** is a change around a living thing that makes it react.
More than one: **stimuli**.

cards.title: Response
body: A **response** is how a living thing **reacts** to the change.

cards.title: Example: a sharp object
body: Move the slider.

states.label: Stimulus
states.text: You step on a sharp object with no shoes. The **pain** is the stimulus.

states.label: Response
states.text: You **jump up** very quickly. That is the response.

cards.title: Receptors and sense organs
body: **Receptors** are special cells and tissues that receive stimuli.
Similar receptors grouped together form a **sense organ**.

cards.title: Memory trick: S then R
body: **S** comes before **R** in the alphabet. The stimulus comes first, then the response.

cards.title: Nice or not nice
body: A stimulus may be **pleasant** or **unpleasant**.
Living things like pleasant stimuli.
They dislike unpleasant stimuli.

cards.title: Activity 8.1: a barking dog
cards.problem: A dog suddenly barks at you. What is the stimulus? What is the response?

steps.text: The change is the sudden **bark** (a sound).
What you do is how you react, for example you jump or run away.

cards.answer: Stimulus: the dog's bark. Response: you jump or move away.

cards.title: Why respond?
body: Plants and animals respond to stimuli to **stay alive** (survive).
Hungry (stimulus) → eat food (response).

cards.title: Outside or inside?
body: A stimulus can come from outside or inside the body. Move the slider.

states.label: Outside
states.text: Stepping on a sharp object is an **outside** (external) stimulus.

states.label: Inside
states.text: Feeling hungry is an **inside** (internal) stimulus.

cards.title: Do plants respond?
body: Yes! Like all living things, plants respond to stimuli.

cards.title: Activity 8.3: a plant near a window (Figure 8.1)

steps.text: Put a pot of straight seedlings near a window.
The shoots bend **towards the light**.
Turn the pot round. Now the shoots point away from the window.
After a day, they bend back **towards the light**.

cards.title: Activity 8.3 answer
body: Stimulus: **light** from one side.
Response: the shoots **grow towards the light**.

cards.title: How plants respond
body: Plants may **wilt**.
They may **lose their leaves**.
They may **grow in a direction**.

cards.title: Slow or fast?

states.label: Plants
states.text: Plants respond to stimuli **slowly**.

states.label: Animals
states.text: Animals respond **much faster** than plants.

cards.title: How animals respond
body: Animals **move the whole body** or **a part** of it.
They move **towards** or **away from** a stimulus.

cards.title: Sense organs
body: **Sense organs** are body parts that receive stimuli.
The **eye** receives light.
The **ear** receives sound.

cards.title: Activity 8.4: think

cards.title: From stimulus to nerve signal
body: Receptors change stimuli into **nerve signals**.
A nerve signal is a **message** sent through nerve tissue.

cards.title: The control centre
body: Nerve signals go to the **control centre**.
The control centre is the **brain** or **spinal cord**.

cards.title: The effector
body: Signals come back from the control centre to the **effector**.
The effector is a **muscle** or a **gland**.
The effector makes the response.

cards.title: The path of a nerve signal (Figure 8.2)
body: Tap each box.
Stimulus → receptor → control centre → effector → response.

cards.title: Activity 8.5: the five sense organs
body: Tap each sense organ to see what it receives.

steps.text: The heat of the flame is the **stimulus**.
The **skin** of the hand is the receptor.
A nerve signal goes to the **spinal cord** and **brain**.
A signal comes back. The arm **muscle** (effector) contracts.
The hand pulls away. This is the **response**.

It is also a **sense organ**.

cards.title: The tongue
body: The tongue is the sense organ of **taste**.
It detects chemicals that **dissolve** (soluble) in the mouth.

cards.title: Four tastes
body: We can identify four tastes:
**sweet, salt, sour and bitter**.

cards.title: Taste regions (Figure 8.5)

cards.title: Good to know

states.text: Wipe your tongue dry. Put sugar on it. Do not mix it with saliva. Can you taste it?

states.label: Why?
states.text: The tongue detects substances that **dissolve**. Dry sugar has not dissolved, so it is hard to taste.

cards.title: The nose
body: The nose is the sense organ of **smell**.
It detects the smell of **gases** in the air.

steps.text: Tiny amounts of a smelly gas are in the air.
The gas goes into the nose.
It **dissolves** in the moist **mucus** inside the nose.
Smell cells on the inner surface sense it. We feel the smell.

cards.title: Smell and taste
body: The sense of smell is **more sensitive** than taste.
With a cold, it is hard to smell.
